result.explanation: A $500 Amazon eGift Card is a gift certificate, which §V.B.1.d prohibits unless it is for employee recognition. In the card's history from Dec 2024 to Mar 2025, I saw no other gift card and no recognition program. The card normally buys office supplies, shipping and telecom. Nothing in the data supports the exception. I did not see the full 461-transaction history.
result.policy_clause: §V.B.1.d — Gift Certificates (except purchases for employee recognition)
result.innocent_explanation: The gift card could have been bought for an employee recognition award. A recognition approval or program record would show that.

result.explanation: Single $4,850 software purchase (SketchUp Pro school licenses, V-Ray) from a software vendor. The card mostly buys software (36 purchases), and the history shows no other Creation Engine charge nearby, so there is no split or double charge. Other software buys follow within days (Rhino, $990). Software is not on the prohibited list and fits the agency's use of this merchant. The amount is the merchant's maximum, but nothing in the data shows a specific problem.
result.innocent_explanation: Departmental purchase of multi-seat design software licenses (SketchUp Pro and V-Ray) for a school or lab, consistent with the card's software buying.

result.explanation: This card buys at QUARTZY almost daily: 615 purchases, mostly lab supplies. Charges of $2,000–$2,400 appear on 2026-02-05 and 02-06 and in December 2025. The merchant references repeat across different days and amounts (e.g. 6020199733904 on Feb 6, 7, 10 and 11), so they look like vendor IDs, not single orders. Descriptions are generic and nothing ties the parts to one need. Total spend is unusually high, but that fits a steady cadence.
result.policy_clause: OMES Internal P-Card Procedures §V.B.1.a — Split Purchasing (known quantity and intent are key)
result.innocent_explanation: Routine daily lab-supply buying through the Quartzy marketplace by a high-volume lab card. Separate orders from different vendors were not known at the time of the first, which is compliant.

result.explanation: Hotel room charges at a hotel that six agencies use, in a normal range (median $1,109.70, max $1,719.71). The card's history shows other business travel: a Best Western stay on 2024-08-28 and parking on the same day. It also pays food-safety organizations (AFDO, BRCGS), which fits a conference trip. The other Hyatt charge that day is a different amount ($1,719.71), so this is not a double charge.
result.innocent_explanation: Conference or travel lodging for official business, with parking on the same date. The two Hyatt charges are likely separate rooms or travelers.

result.explanation: The description reads "Annual Pope Tech Web Accessibility" with a 5% discount, which is a business software subscription for a university. The card has two Pope Tech charges of exactly $3,420, which fits a yearly renewal. The window I pulled showed only the 2024-07-03 charge, so I didn't see the second charge's date. No split, double charge, or prohibited or personal category appears.
result.innocent_explanation: Annual renewal of a web accessibility testing subscription, charged once a year at the same amount.

result.explanation: Four Amazon charges on 2024-02-19, same marketplace seller reference (S821H21P3) and identical description, total $10,871.04. Each is under $5,000, but the combined total is over the limit. This is the card's first activity, so there is no history of steady similar-size buying. The card's median purchase is $121.40. Nothing in the data explains it as routine.
result.policy_clause: OMES Internal P-Card Procedures §V.B.1.a — Split Purchasing: dividing a quantity or failing to consolidate a known quantity to evade the $5,000 limit
result.innocent_explanation: Separate needs ordered from the same seller on one day, or several unrelated line items billed separately. An order or invoice would show this.

result.explanation: Three same-day charges at WINSUPPLY C, each under $5,000 (4,341.56; 3,804.57; 4,631.15), total $12,777.28, with identical "GENERAL PURCHASE" descriptions.
